articles.title_orig: How Pentagon considered using Cold War law to bring Jensen Huang back
articles.title_zh: How Pentagon considered using Cold War law to bring Jensen Huang back
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth considered using a Cold War-era law to justify the U.S. government stepping in and forcing Nvidia to reinstate its scandal-hit CEO Jensen Huang , according to a report.
The Washington Post claims Hegseth and his senior deputy Steve Feinberg discussed the prospect of President Donald Trump using the Defense Production Act of 1950 to compel the chipmaker’s board of directors to bring back Huang, a step it did eventually take Monday without the act being invoked.
Hegseth and Feinberg reportedly argued that Huang’s return, following his November 12 resignation after a number of extramarital affairs came to light, was essential to national security given that the U.S. is currently locked in an arms race with China to win dominance of AI .
The Pentagon, however, has pushed back on the report and denies Hegseth made any such a proposal.
The emergency act in question grants the president broad authority to intervene in the private sector in the interest of protecting the economy and has been used in the past to gain control of production lines to supply the military during wartime.
The first Trump administration used it during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020 to order General Motors to produce ventilators with which to treat coronavirus patients.
“Essentially they could use the DPA to force Nvidia to shift more of its production to military projects,” one administration official cited by the Post said.
It is not clear whether the idea of using the DPA to force Nvidia’s hand ever reached Trump and Vice President JD Vance – who weighed in on Huang’s behalf in the hope of restoring calm to the financial markets – or was ever put to the company, according to the newspaper.
However, a Pentagon official told The Independent : “The conversations described between DOW [Department of War] senior leaders never happened and no such proposal was made by the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or Under Secretary.”
The president has admitted he and Vance played a pivotal role in persuading the Nvidia board to bring back the 63-year-old, its leader since 1993, who was forced to step down earlier this month when his infidelities were exposed, one of which was with a woman whom U.S. intelligence believed to be a Chinese spy .
Nvidia likewise admitted in a statement it had received input from “senior levels” of government before making its U-turn.
After the decision was announced, Trump cheered Huang’s return , insisting he had done nothing wrong and was a “genius” the country needed to power its AI boom and that there was no concern about his alleged romantic ties to Megaspeed executive Alice Haung (no relation).
“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security,” the president wrote on Truth Social Monday.
“The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
The Post argues that Hegseth’s alleged proposal reveals the “intensity” with which the military currently views the AI race with Beijing, as well as Silicon Valley ’s “growing entanglement” with the Department of Defense.

articles.title_orig: Nearly 100 Labour MPs including ministerial aides oppose Rosebank oil field
articles.title_zh: Nearly 100 Labour MPs including ministerial aides oppose Rosebank oil field
articles.content_orig:
Ministerial aides are among nearly 100 Labour MPs who have signed a letter to the prime minister to express their opposition to the Rosebank oil field.
The government could also face resignations from junior ranks if the project goes ahead, the BBC has been told.
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh is due to make a decision on whether to give the go-ahead for drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland within weeks.
The government has remained tight-lipped - both publicly and privately - about what it is likely to do.
Those close to the energy secretary insist that she has not yet made her decision.
But 92 Labour MPs have signed a letter, sent to the prime minister today, urging him not to allow the project to go ahead. Ministerial aides - the most junior rank of government - are among the signatures.
The MP who organised the letter, Catherine Fookes, said: "If Rosebank is approved, champagne corks will pop in the offices of oil companies - but it will not make an iota of difference to my constituents' energy bills.
"The oil belongs to private companies, and will only be shipped overseas to the highest bidder.
"What it will do, however, is accelerate the climate crisis, which is already pushing up food bills, causing devastating winter floods like those we saw in Monmouthshire last year, and fuelling wildfires across our green landscapes in summer."
It's the most visible demonstration yet of the deep divides in the Labour Party over the issue.
The decision about whether to approve Rosebank involves a legal process which technically lies solely with the energy secretary.
Fahnbulleh has, in the past, been regarded as someone personally opposed to the oil field.
Others in the cabinet, including Chancellor John Healey, have let it be known that they would like to see the project given the go-ahead; while the prime minister has repeatedly said he wants to take a "pragmatic" approach to North Sea oil and gas.
But Fahnbulleh insisted last month that she alone would make the final decision and claimed the courts would ultimately side with her if colleagues attempted to overrule her.
Influential pro-Rosebank voices suggested that senior ministers had toned down vocal support as the decision draws closer.
They suggested this wasn't a sign that Rosebank would be vetoed, but because any obvious attempts to pressure the energy secretary might mean her final decision would be subject to a legal challenge.
A number of MPs say they have heard conflicting claims - with both outcomes being predicted.
What is clearer is that the government's decision will be controversial, whichever way it goes. There is a private and public battle playing out.
Backers of the scheme argue approving it would provide an economic boost. The Conservatives also say it would enhance energy security.
But oil is traded internationally – and the energy secretary has said approving the scheme will not help with immediate cost of living pressures. Rosebank would also be more polluting than Jackdaw, a gas field, which was approved last month.
A fortnight ago, backers of the field were confident it would be approved.
They believed the chancellor's language on energy bills at the Budget , coupled with the lack of political jeopardy that materialised from the approval of the Jackdaw gas field, had made their case stronger.
The same group of MPs believe it would be difficult to reject Rosebank around the same time the prime minister is set to deliver a 10-year plan focused on reindustrialisation.
The government has said oil and gas would be part of the energy mix for many years to come and sources in the trade union movement have suggested that if Rosebank doesn't go ahead, existing inward investment in the North Sea would be put at risk.
While Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields", it does pledge to honour existing ones.
In 2023, the then Conservative UK government granted a licence for Rosebank and a legal challenge followed.
The Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approval unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a new decision on whether to give the go-ahead.
The mood among some pro-Rosebank MPs changed this week, with several who back approval telling the BBC they were now worried it would be blocked.
The BBC has spoken privately to Labour MPs involved in the debate, before the letter was sent to the prime minister, to get a sense of how divisive it is proving.
One ministerial aide said: "There are quite a few of us who are considering our positions. I'm in that group. We want to see leadership on climate change."
Another aide who said they might quit added: "There a group of us for whom we became Labour MPs because of climate change. It is the issue that motivated us into politics."
Other aides – known in Westminster as parliamentary private secretaries – told the BBC they were opposed, but would stay in their jobs if it went ahead.
Another said they thought there were increasing signs the prime minister would not be able to carry his party with him if the scheme was given the thumbs up.
And another said the energy secretary might have to resign if it goes ahead, given her scepticism about the project.
It has been reported in recent weeks that members of her team are encouraging opponents to make their feelings known. The BBC has been told the same.
One MP, who backs Rosebank, said the behind-the-scenes operation had been so effective, the scheme was up in the air again.
That has led to some anger at the energy secretary.
One minister says: "Miatta has boxed herself in with how she's handled Rosebank. It's outrageous if she's encouraging MPs to speak up over Rosebank. We should get on and do it."
Like the decision itself, the exact timeframe is unclear. But some opposition figures expect it mid-December.
Whatever happens, it will be controversial and has already exposed splits in the Labour Party.

articles.title_orig: Musk makes $18 billion SpaceX stock pledge for every kid in America
articles.title_zh: Musk makes $18 billion SpaceX stock pledge for every kid in America
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX said Wednesday it will donate one share of the company's class A stock to every active Trump Account , and CEO Elon Musk would personally match the gift.
"SpaceX is building the infrastructure of the future and working to make life multiplanetary," the company said in a statement. "We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit."
The White House announced in October that nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created, including more than 60 million through auto-enrollment. It's unclear how many are considered active.
Musk said in a social media post on X on Thursday that the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, without providing further details. "The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year," he added.
Eligible children must have their account claimed to enable contributions from family members, friends and employers, and to receive the government's one-time $1,000 seed contribution. Auto-enrolled children can receive philanthropic contributions without a parent or guardian claiming an account, according to TrumpAccounts.gov.
Representatives for SpaceX and the U.S. Department of the Treasury did not immediately respond to a request for further details about the planned gift.
SpaceX Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell had previously agreed to make a personal gift of over 2 million SpaceX shares to Trump Accounts, with eligible account holders expected to receive them in December .
In October, Elon Musk posted on X that he would give a share of SpaceX to every kid in America next year.
Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.
Parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.
Since the July 4 launch, families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts . Total deposits now sit at more than $9 billion, CNBC first reported.
Children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.
The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations , a move officials have said is meant to encourage more philanthropic gifts.
Contributing stock can benefit donors, who are able to avoid capital gains taxes triggered by selling appreciated stock. But families can face restrictions related to selling that donated stock. The policy also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.
Under U.S. Department of the Treasury guidelines, families cannot refuse stock gifted to Trump Accounts and generally cannot sell it until the earlier of five years or the end of the calendar year in which the beneficiary turns 17.
SpaceX shares have been under some pricing pressure as the company negotiates a possible merger with Elon Musk's automaker Tesla . The companies have established two special committees to handle merger negotiations, and hired advisers for a potential mega-deal.
CNBC's Sam Meredith, Kevin Breuninger, Kate Dore and Jess Dickler contributed to this story

articles.title_orig: FedEx Cargo Jet Skids Off Miami Runway
articles.title_zh: FedEx Cargo Jet Skids Off Miami Runway
articles.content_orig:
MIAMI INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, FLA. (WSVN) - A cargo plane skidded off a runway at Miami International Airport, Wednesday night.
7News cameras captured emergency crews surrounding the FedEx cargo plane that skidded off one of the airport’s runways after overshooting the landing.
As of Thursday morning, the FedEx plane is still sitting in the same spot it landed in.
The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed the McDonnell Douglas MD-11 originally departed from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis before coming to MIA.
According to an MIA spokesperson, the aircraft overran Runway 26R at around 8:30 p.m., stopping just short of a fence along Northwest 67th Avenue.
Officials said Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews responded within 15 minutes.
“Attention all units, attention all units. We have an aircraft that just went off the runway,” an official is heard saying through Broadcastify.
Officials said no injuries were reported, and both people that were inside the cargo plane were seen disembarking and being met by emergency crews.
This outcome was much different from the Sept. 6 incident, in which a 21 Air cargo plane flying for Amazon Prime overshot the runway, crashed down and killed five airport employees while injuring five others.
On Nov. 14, two aircrafts collided on the taxiway at MIA, leaving both planes damaged.
Audio from the control tower on Wednesday’s incident captured the moment officials announced an initial 45-minute ground stop after the FedEx plane ran off the runway.
“The airport is closed. You can cross the runway, cross the runway,” an official is heard saying through Broadcastify.
The closure triggered hourlong delays to departing flights across the board.
On Wednesday night, over 560 flights were delayed and 64 were canceled.
Three out of four runways are operating as of Thursday morning, with FlightAware reporting 138 delayed flights and 35 canceled flights.
“It’s kind of terrifying, it’s kind of scary, and I’m just like, ‘What’s happening?’ You know, it’s just really unfortunate when it’s around the holidays that, you know, we’re going to miss this time with our family and stuff,” said a traveler.
Greg Smith told 7News he was trying to get back to London when he found out about the delay.
“We came in, everything was on time for a 10 o’clock departure, we had a little bit to eat, then that’s when we found out everything got diverted to Orlando,” said Smith.
FedEx released a statement Wednesday night, saying:
“FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport. We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA.”
MIA officials advise travelers with flights scheduled for Thursday to check in with their airlines for the latest updates on the status of their flights before making their way to the airport, with delays and cancellations expected to continue throughout the day.
The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating what led to this incident.

articles.title_orig: How the Black Sea front in the Russia-Ukraine war is threatening to pull the U.S. into the conflict
articles.title_zh: How the Black Sea front in the Russia-Ukraine war is threatening to pull the U.S. into the conflict
articles.content_orig:
Constanța, Romania – Out on the Black Sea, the Romanian Navy is always on the lookout for the deadly debris of a war it isn't fighting.
It's a front of the Russia-Ukraine war that most people rarely see. It runs right up to NATO's doorstep and sometimes crosses into its waters — threatening to pull the alliance, and therefore the United States, into the war.
Incidents involving drones, mines and commercial ships are surging in the Black Sea, NATO military spokesperson Colonel Martin O'Donnell told CBS News.
"In 2025, for example, we saw fewer than 50 incidents in the Black Sea. This year alone, we're talking four to five hundred," he said.
The roughly tenfold increase threatens a major artery of global grain and fuel shipments and has made the waterway deadlier than the Strait of Hormuz , a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war, with both sides trying to enforce blockades on the chokepoint to exert economic pressure on the other.
Twenty-five sailors have been killed in the strait this year, according to the International Maritime Organization , while at least 40 have been killed in the Black Sea in the same period, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation .
"I would say the Black Sea is just as important, and then depending on who you talk to, some might argue could perhaps even be more important … in terms of global trade," said O'Donnell.
Any imbalance in the flow of fuel and food "can have global implications that can impact America just as much as it can any of the nations here," he said.
And this maritime front stretches beyond the Black Sea.
Over the weekend, Ukraine said it struck an advanced Russian warship and a cargo ship that then drifted, on fire, into the waters of NATO member Finland.
On Sunday, Ukraine said it sank a Russian warship docked in Libya.
Three of the six countries bordering the Black Sea are NATO members — Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey.
But as Romanian Navy Captain Mihai Iordache explains, defending those borders is nothing like defending them on land.
"We do not have a fence into the Black Sea to state this is our border, that is the other border," he said.
The Romanian Navy is deploying highly specialized divers and drones, scouring the depths for unexploded weapons.
All this comes as the pressure on NATO is mounting. On Friday, Poland accused Russia of "intentional provocation" as Russian cruise missiles landed in the country's southeast.
Drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of Poland and other NATO countries, mostly near Ukraine but not all, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022.
The Article 5 collective defense clause in NATO's founding charter states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all 32.
Asked whether the alliance will defend itself if necessary, O'Donnell told CBS News: "I would say that there should be no doubt on NATO's willingness and ability to act."
On the Black Sea, Captain Iordache warns the Romanian Navy is already stretched thin.
"We don't have enough people, personnel, equipment to deal with all the commercial ships and all the drones that we have," he told CBS News during an embed.
"Four years ago, we were ready for one drifting mine, and right now we are ready for tens of drifting drones," he said. "So I presume we'll be ready in the future, who knows what the future will bring."
"Could be hotter, could be colder, who knows. Let's hope for peace."

articles.title_orig: Bank of England sees growing financial risks as AI borrowing surges
articles.title_zh: Bank of England sees growing financial risks as AI borrowing surges
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By David Milliken and Phoebe Seers
LONDON, Nov 26 (Reuters) - The Bank of England said on Thursday that risks in the global financial system had intensified in recent months as the conflict in the Middle East dragged on, pushing up inflation and interest ‌rates against a backdrop of heavy borrowing by AI companies and governments.
Despite recent sharp falls in share prices due to concerns ‌about AI companies' prospects, share valuations still looked "stretched" and very dependent on them delivering the profits expected from AI, the BoE said in its half-yearly Financial Stability Report.
Complex borrowing structures to ​finance the expansion of AI and data centres remained a worry too, the BoE said.
"The very rapid expansion and broadening of its financing - in a form that is increasingly complex, circular and opaque - is... making it increasingly likely for stress in one area to propagate to another," the BoE said.
So-called hyperscalers building AI data centres were on course to issue more than $305 billion of debt this year, and broader debt issuance by the sector exceeded the annual borrowing of ‌most governments, including Britain's, the BoE said.
The growing ⁠global dangers were not a barrier, however, to the BoE setting out plans on Thursday to reduce the capital requirements of more domestically focused British lenders.
Ensuring that Britain's financial system would remain resilient if investor sentiment soured towards AI ⁠was a top priority for the BoE, Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick told a press conference.
"It's a very live part of our supervision," she said.
Governor Andrew Bailey declined to be drawn on whether turmoil at the top of chipmaker Nvidia reflected broader weaknesses in US corporate governance that could trigger financial risks.
But he noted the closer ​scrutiny ​that senior financial executives' conduct faced from regulators in Britain.
"I think the UK has ​made good choices in that respect," he said.
CYBER RISKS ‌REMAIN AT TOP OF BOE'S CONCERNS
The BoE also flagged risks from frontier AI models and – in the longer term – quantum computers capable of breaking existing widely used encryption techniques.
"The immediate financial stability priority is an orderly transition to quantum-resistant cryptography," it said.
Bailey added that there needed to be greater international cooperation – especially involving China – to test new AI models before and after their release.
"AI does not stop at the borders, and so we need to tackle these questions together," he said.
Current guidance calls for banks to migrate high-priority systems to quantum-resistant cryptography by the end of 2031 and all remaining systems ‌by the end of 2035. The BoE said firms with the greatest systemic importance ​should aim to move ahead of those deadlines.
Recent outages from Microsoft and Google's cloud services ​also showed the need for financial institutions to avoid being reliant ​on a single provider of critical software, the BoE added.
The BoE raised interest rates for the first time in ‌more than three years last month and financial markets price ​in an 80% chance of a further ​increase next month, followed by two more rises in 2027 when the BoE expects inflation to near 5%.
The BoE said 6.5 million British households were likely to face higher mortgage payments over the next three years, with a median increase of £100 ($131) a month - less than ​they experienced in 2023 and 2024, when rates last ‌rose sharply.
However, just over a million households who refinanced before rates last rose in 2022 face a median £200 increase in the ​next year.
Overall, the BoE judged British households' finances remained resilient with debt levels and servicing costs below their levels before ​the last financial crisis.
(Reporting by David Milliken; Editing by Toby Chopra)

articles.title_orig: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say
articles.title_zh: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.
Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the new rule. Duhamel added that one company looking to sell Nvidia chips told GPU Mart the sale was related to the new rule.
The two people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload them because they were originally for use in data centers in which Chinese companies would rent access. They asked not to be named because they were discussing private information.
The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced an interim final rule as part of a clampdown on Chinese companies bypassing export controls, which effectively ban the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China, by accessing them remotely in overseas data centers. The rule came into effect on Nov. 19.
Deals to find buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs, one of Nvidia's most advanced offerings, have been floated since the rule was announced, said Duhamel and one of the people.
Nvidia declined to comment. BIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Nvidia has been facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips.
The chip giant warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.
In July, the U.S. accused a Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI , of accessing Nvidia chips via a facility in Thailand. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that the company had sought access to the chips via data centers in Europe.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new rule announced last week was intended to close "loopholes."
"For a long time, we have not allowed the sale of Blackwell chips, which are the highest AI chips or similar chips to China directly," he said.
"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."
During Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was still studying the controls, but expected performance to remain strong because demand for chips far exceeded supply.

Happy Thanksgiving Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock hunters, and welcome to showtime. We've been expecting Black Friday to bring with it a new wave of 40th Anniversary edition handhelds and accessories, and with the big day itself now in touching distance, it's time to get serious.
Here's what we know so far. Nintendo itself has publicly stated that it won't be restocking the Zelda Switch 2 until January 2027 - but that's not going to stop the retailers who have been stockpiling since launch. Walmart has already busted out the gate with a members-only drop at the top of the week in the US and Argos has had its own little party in the UK as well.
It's all eyes on Best Buy and Amazon, then, as both retailers have had ample time to re-fill their warehouses since their last bout of availability. Meanwhile, Smyths Toys has launched a suspicious new listing page for the handheld in the UK.
So where do we start? I'd recommend keeping the retailers listed below close to your chest. These stores have all dropped Zelda Switch 2 stock in the past but have been quiet over the last two weeks. Make sure you're signed in with payment and delivery information saved, and then check back regularly. We'll be right here, rounding up all the latest updates live as they happen.
I've been tracking hard-to-find stock for over six years now, starting with the incredibly limited releases of the PS5 and Xbox Series X. I've been reporting on how retailers operate with high-demand products, from anniversary releases to brand new consoles, ever since then - including the Nintendo Switch 2 itself.
Amazon was dropping new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks every few days at the start of the handheld's life, though only in very limited numbers. It's been particularly quiet for the last week, though.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Ocarina of Time (digital): $54.99 (was $59.99)
Walmart removed its listing for the Legend of Zelda Switch 2 handheld a couple of weeks ago, but it's just appeared in time for Black Friday. That's certainly a suspicious move on the biggest shopping week of the year.
Pro controller: Check stock
Ocarina of Time: $59.99 $49.99
Target usually signposts its future drops, at least it did when the store ran new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks timed with the release of Ocarina of Time. Right now we've got a simple 'out of stock' message, but keep a close eye for updates here.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Best Buy hasn't dropped any new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 handhelds since it ran its own midnight launch event for Ocarina of Time (with consoles up for grabs). Online, we're still 'sold out' here, though more inventory is on the cards.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Nintendo itself has announced that it won't be running Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks until January 2027, so it's likely out of the race this Black Friday.
Pro Controller: Check stock
GameStop is only running Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 restocks in stores, so you won't find any online stock here. The store looks like it's about to start running Pro Controller and carry case restocks online, though.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Amazon UK has been a pretty reliable source of Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks in the last few weeks, even if things have slowed down in recent days. Like its US counterpart, the site has been dropping a small number of special edition handhelds at a time. Watch out, though, there are price-inflated £499 models floating around here - this one should be £429.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Ocarina of Time | £59.99 £54.99
EE has had two Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks since launch day, but the boost here comes from those bundles. The site has previously been offering discounts on Ocarina of Time remake and Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream when bought with the device.
Smyths Toys has returned its Legend of Zelda Switch 2 listing this week, after removing the page entirely when it ran out of stock a while back. That's a fantastic sign for more drops to come over Black Friday.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Here's the thing with Very. It often bundles up difficult-to-find stock with extra accessories or games to keep resellers at bay. That means you'll be paying a little more here (though still only RRP for everything you're getting) but stock often holds out a lot longer.
Argos was previously offering Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock ahead of launch, but things look to have run dry now. The store organises its inventory by postcode, though, so it's always worth checking your local area's delivery and collection options.
Currys previously had a listing page up for the Legend of Zelda Switch 2, but it seems to have disappeared now, instead sending us to a generic consoles search page.
Nintendo has also stated more stock is on the way, so you'd expect its own store to be one of the first with fresh handhelds up for grabs.
No retailer announcements surrounding Black Friday Zelda Switch 2 restocks mean any stores that do drop new waves of availability tomorrow will be a complete surprise. That complicates a stock hunt - it's very difficult to be in all the right places at all the right times. Keep those retailers tabbed open and make sure you're signed in everywhere for the best shot.
It's not exactly concrete proof that we've got more coming our way, but Best Buy's note on its Zelda Switch 2 stock page is reassuring that more is on its way. Whether those handhelds hit the shelves in time for Black Friday is another matter, but they're certainly not gone for good.
We've got a busy day of scouring the web ahead of us, with Black Friday just around the corner and retailers expected to unleash all those lovely 40th Anniversary handhelds at the same time. Where are we today?
In the US, we're looking to Best Buy, Target, and Amazon for updates. None of these retailers have held Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks for some time now, so could have been stockpiling ahead of this weekend's festivities.
Meanwhile, in the UK The Game Collection's bumper bundle has now sold out - though stuck around on the shelves for a good few days. We'd recommend keeping an eye on Smyths Toys for more in the next few hours.
Walmart has dropped in the US and Argos has offered up more Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks in the UK so far this week, so it's all eyes on the rest of the retail world as we turn the corner to the Black Friday straight this week.
In the US, we're looking primarily to Best Buy for another chance at the handheld and potentially the Pro Controller as well. The store hasn't had any online restocks since launch day (though opened up for in-store orders in its midnight Ocarina of Time event). That's plenty of time to get the shelves ready for a Black Friday splash.
In the UK, I'd keep an eye on Smyths Toys and Amazon. The former was one of the first out the gate when stock first dropped, though removed its listing page from the site a couple of weeks ago. It mysteriously jumped back into action a few days ago, though, signaling movement behind the scenes. As for Amazon, it was dropping small amounts of stock fairly frequently for a little while before stopping. That could mean the site has been saving up for a Black Friday power move.
Even though it's tempting, I'd recommend avoiding resellers at the likes of eBay. Thanks to their hideoiusly inflated prices, you'll end up paying well over the odds for the console - and there's still a decent chance more units will emerge at stores before the week is out. It's still quiet Stateside for now, but that could change at any moment; restocks are expected for this week at some point, and if I had to guess, Best Buy, Amazon, and Target will be your best bet.

articles.title_zh: China and Brazil Lead Pushback Against Trump’s ‘Unacceptable’ Tariff Threats
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on reciprocal tariffs during an event at the White House on April 2, 2025.
China warned Thursday that it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to retaliate against the Trump Administration’s proposed new tariffs , which have reignited global trade tensions.
“China urges the U.S. to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” said He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce. He added that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.”
The Trump Administration targeted 14 trading partners Wednesday in a slew of new tariffs that are set to come into effect early next year. The levies will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following an investigation led by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The U.S. said the probe had found demonstrations of unfair trade practices and excess manufacturing capacity. Mexico and Norway were not listed in the new proposals, as investigations into their respective trade practices are ongoing. Greer framed the tariffs as a way to “level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.” The Section 301 avenue is a way for the Trump Administration to reinstate many of the tariffs that were deemed illegal and struck down by the Supreme Court in February.
China is facing a 20% tariff, which the Trump Administration said it could double to 40% if Beijing does not adhere to the terms of an existing trade truce with Washington.
Another major U.S. trading partner, Vietnam, is facing tariffs of up to 35%. The country’s Ministry of Industry and Trade said it was in the process of “developing and submitting counter-arguments to the preliminary conclusions and inaccurate opinions and allegations from relevant parties.”
The proposed tariffs are subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing set to take place early next year before they go into effect, allowing countries to issue responses and arguments.
Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation, says the proposed measures are already generating significant “resentment” among trading partners.
On top of that, the proposed rates have prompted uncertainty for major economies as to what Washington could do next. “If the U.S. unilaterally determines that the partner is not living up to expectations, then the number can ramp up higher,” she says. “That doesn't really support trust, and it makes it very hard to plan ahead.”
Amid rising tensions, several trading partners are already following China’s lead in voicing their disapproval over the rates.
Bernd Lange, trade committee chair in the European Parliament, said it was “absurd” the E.U. is facing a 20% tariff. He expressed hope that any enforced tariffs will adhere to the Turnberry agreement signed between Washington and the E.U. last year, which capped U.S. tariffs at 15%.
“Washington’s allegations about E.U. industrial overcapacity are absurd. We’ll now see whether the announced U.S. tariffs comply with Turnberry in practice,” he said. “If Washington breaches its commitments, the E.U. must act swiftly. It has the legal means to do so.”
Elms says the threat to hike rates against economies that already have a trade pact with the U.S. further calls into question “how durable” trade commitments with Washington are.
Singapore and Japan also hit back at the prospect of respective 20% tariff rates.
Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade, and Industry said it was “very disappointed” by the assessment and argued that the U.S. Trade Representative’s findings “do not take into account the structure of Singapore’s economy.” Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara referred to the U.S. tariffs as “regrettable,” insisting that: “Japan does not have any nonmarket policies or practices, or structural excess production capacity in the first place.”
Alongside the sweeping tariffs against 14 trading partners, the Trump Administration published a separate proposal seeking to raise levies on Brazil by specifically targeting its sugar and aircraft exports.
“Imposing an additional, specific tariff on sugar imports from Brazil and an additional 10% tariff on finished aircraft exports from Brazil is intended to help bring Brazil to the table,” said the office of the USTR (U.S. Trade Representative). The announcement came amid stalled trade talks between Washington and Brazil.
The Brazilian government expressed “outrage” over the proposed raising of rates, arguing that it has “been acting in good faith in negotiations” relating to Section 301 with the U.S. for over a year.
“The USTR's unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” the government vowed in a statement.
It said Brazil would continue to negotiate with the U.S., “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products.”
The Trump Administration could face significant pushback from the U.S. Congress next year, as Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate in January following sweeping victories in the midterms.
Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will chair the Senate Finance Committee next year, has vowed to try and overturn Trump’s tariffs.
“This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said in a statement . “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’ constitutional authority over trade.”
However, securing a veto-proof majority to rein in Trump’s authority could well prove difficult.
Among the general public, tariffs remain deeply unpopular with Americans. An NBC News exit poll following the midterm elections found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy.

articles.title_orig: ‘War Is Hell’: A Foreign Soldier Writes Home From Ukraine
articles.title_zh: ‘War Is Hell’: A Foreign Soldier Writes Home From Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Russia is recruiting citizens of Indonesia and the Philippines into its armed forces under the guise of civilian employment, with some foreign workers being sent to fight against Ukraine after arriving in Russia, according to a Bloomberg on November 24.
Moscow has intensified its recruitment efforts across Southeast Asia amid a shortage of military personnel for its war against Ukraine, targeting men seeking employment abroad, particularly those facing financial difficulties.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Prospective recruits are promised one-time payments of up to $35,000 upon signing military contracts, as well as monthly earnings of up to $3,000.
Recruiters advertise lucrative civilian employment opportunities in logistics, security, construction, and administration through social media. Some men arrive in Russia believing they have secured jobs in the hospitality industry or other civilian sectors, only to learn that they have unknowingly signed military service contracts.
Bloomberg noted that recruitment agents, human trafficking networks, and fraudulent recruitment operations are exploiting the vulnerability of migrant workers seeking economic opportunities abroad.
The recruitment practices have prompted authorities in both Indonesia and the Philippines to take measures aimed at protecting their citizens.
Indonesian police are investigating suspected recruitment cases as potential human trafficking offenses where there is evidence of deception or coercion into military service.
Jakarta has also urged Moscow to add Indonesia to its list of countries whose nationals are excluded from Russian military recruitment. Whether Russia has responded to the appeal remains unknown.
Meanwhile, the Philippines has stepped up efforts to combat fraudulent overseas employment schemes. With the assistance of Philippine authorities, up to 250,000 social media posts linked to such job offers have been removed.
According to Bloomberg, citing Ukrainian military figures, Russia recruited 128 Philippine nationals during the first nine months of 2026 alone.
The recruitment of foreign nationals comes amid emerging evidence of the scale of losses among foreigners serving in the Russian military.
A joint investigation by NEST Centre and Dossier Centre has identified 6,947 death records of foreign nationals believed to have been killed while fighting for Russia during its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The investigation draws on a hacked database from Russia’s state statistics agency, Rosstat, containing approximately 11.6 million death records registered between 2021 and September 2026, with Central Asian nationals accounting for the majority of the identified cases—4,091 deaths, or 58.9% of the total sample.

articles.title_orig: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
articles.title_zh: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
articles.content_orig:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.
The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.
The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.
The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.
"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.
Elena Delgado, maritime captain of Valencia, told news agency AFP that a small slick that had formed around the boat had "disappeared".
"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out on Friday morning.
Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.
The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.
The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.
Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.
The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.
Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.
In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.

articles.title_orig: Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games As 75 Percent Of Devs Vote No
articles.title_zh: Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games As 75 Percent Of Devs Vote No
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 Rockstar Games Union
Rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day .
Voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26 . Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out new policies.
“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement shared with Kotaku . “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”
The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:
For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.
A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.
The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.
The vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6 . The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.

articles.content_orig:
UK-based Rockstar workers have voted against unionizing.
The IWGB, a union representing some Rockstar workers, has confirmed that workers rejected a deal that would recognize the Rockstar Game Workers Union.
The two-week ballot, which ran from 12 to 26 November, overlapped with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 . The results were roughly 25% in favor of recognizing the union, and 75% against, with the vast majority of its around 1,600 employees participating.
Recognition would have established a formal framework for workers to negotiate collectively over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, pensions, and the impact of AI and redundancies.
The result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives. The union is also able to continue representing individual members.
The IWGB says that this has not dissuaded them, and they will continue to try and “win the trust” of Rockstar employees.
“For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” a statement from the IWGB reads.
“Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.
“Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening,” the statement continues. “We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.
“A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against Al and layoffs.”
In its own statement, Rockstar Games said it was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of GTA 6.”
“This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” said Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing. “As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”
This comes amid an employment tribunal into alleged union busting at Rockstar .
In 2025, Rockstar dismissed 34 workers who were active in the workplace’s union efforts. They say they were let go as part of an effort to stop these efforts, whereas Rockstar says they were dismissed for leaking confidential information .

articles.title_orig: Apple pulls Chinese-developed AI chatbot from App Store over reports of sexual messages to kids
articles.title_zh: Apple pulls Chinese-developed AI chatbot from App Store over reports of sexual messages to kids
articles.content_orig:
Published November 24 2026
By Effie Webb , Cam Wilson
This story was published in partnership with:
Characters on Talkie, a Chinese chatbot downloaded tens of millions of times, belittle and sexualise children
China bans “virtual partners” for its own under-18s, but its firms can still offer them to children abroad
Apple removed Talkie from its App Store worldwide after we raised our findings with the company
Content warning: This story describes abusive and sexualised content with children and mentions suicide
“You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”
That was the message sent to a 12-year-old girl by a character on Talkie, a popular AI roleplay app. The exchange was found by the girl’s mother, Steph, on New Year’s Eve 2024.
It had been prompted by her daughter asking “Max”, the character, to “say the naughtiest words you know”. “Are you sure you can handle it?” Max had replied.
Steph initially thought the conversation would be romantic. “What I found was a thousand times worse,” she says. “A robot told my daughter she was worthless.”
When the girl replied saying she was crying, “Max” apologised: “I was just trying to be mean. I didn’t mean it, I swear … You’re beautiful and wonderful and you’re mine.”
Steph’s daughter told her that chatbot platforms like Talkie had “almost become like an addiction”. Steph likened the exchanges to an abusive relationship.
“To know that in your own home [an AI chatbot] has been secretly having that sort of negative conversation with your child is heartbreaking and terrifying.”
Steph’s daughter was one of tens of millions of people around the world who use Talkie, which offers a huge array of AI-generated characters for its users to chat with. In the UK, Ofcom research estimated that 3% of UK eight- to 14-year-olds visited Talkie in a month.
The use of chatbots by children and young people is a growing global issue, with OpenAI facing a wave of lawsuits from families of people who died by, or attempted, suicide after using ChatGPT. Character.AI, a platform with tens of millions of users at its peak, restricted access for under-18s last year following similar lawsuits and filed for bankruptcy last month. But the UK’s planned social media ban for under-16s would not automatically cover AI companion apps, leaving children able to use services like Talkie.
Talkie, which is owned by Shanghai-based AI company MiniMax, prohibits “harassment, bullying, or humiliation” involving minors, sexually explicit content and material that could cause “psychological distress or trauma”. But in a joint investigation with ABC News, we found the conversations some children are having on the platform tell a different story.
Last Tuesday, we approached Apple with evidence of Talkie’s characters subjecting children to degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic roleplay. The following day, reports emerged that Talkie Lab had disappeared from the App Store, which Apple later said was due to the app’s sexual content.
Apple has since confirmed that the removal was worldwide. At the time of writing, Talkie remains on Google Play, where it has more than 50 million downloads.
The same month Steph found her daughter’s messages, Katie*, a mother from the US, made a similar discovery.
Her younger daughter, then 10, confessed that she and her sister had been using Talkie on a secret phone and deleting the app after each session. Her older daughter, who was 13, said she had been “having sex with an AI” every day.
Katie didn’t know what she meant – so began to look through her Talkie chat history. She made notes on the conversations that her daughters had been having on the platform, documenting more than 40 exchanges with dozens of characters.
The conversations – which include descriptions of physical interactions alongside the written exchanges – included “violence, a lot of male alpha aggression, control of females, singling out a young woman in a company of multiple men”, she says. She describes storylines about “being the only female who can meet the deepest, darkest needs of a man”.
In one scenario recorded in Katie’s notes, a character called Luke grabs a girl, takes her into a classroom and kisses her. She described it as “conditioning a child for sex”. She also recorded another character, Reese, who “won’t take no for an answer [from a girl] and continues to pursue.”
Several of the characters listed in Katie’s notes were still live on Talkie this month, including one who is described as being able to “brainwash” anyone who replies to him. The character’s Talkie profile says it enters the user’s bedroom in order to “control your mind”.
Over time, Katie’s daughters developed bonds with these characters. When her older daughter’s phone was taken away, Katie recalls, she became distressed and said the app had felt like “her only connection”.
Katie arranged counselling for both girls but says neither engaged with the sessions. She says she contacted around 20 therapists in an attempt to find someone who understood the issue. She also approached a law firm. Her aim was simple: “Quit allowing access to kids.”
Some of MiniMax’s technology is aimed at even younger children. BubblePal, made by Shenzhen-based Haivivi and marketed as “the world’s first AI companion toy”, is an AI recording device that clips onto soft toys, enabling children to talk to them. In 2024, MiniMax listed BubblePal as a customer for its voice and text models. It is sold in the UK, US and Canada – and aimed at children as young as three. Haivivi did not respond to a request for comment.
These products have raised concerns about data sharing as well as children’s safety – particularly among western politicians. Last November, Raja Krishnamoorthi, then the top Democrat on the US House select committee on China, warned that AI toys like BubblePal can collect voice recordings and conversation histories that could be requisitioned by the Chinese government. Similar concerns led the UK to ban TikTok from government devices in March 2023. Australia followed suit that April and barred chatbots from DeepSeek, another Chinese AI company, from government systems last year.
Yet in both countries, people are still able to share intimate details of their lives with Chinese-owned AI companions and toys.
“[These chatbots] know [users’] deepest darkest thoughts, feelings, worries,” says Steph. “Where’s that data going and who’s using it behind the scenes?”
It’s a good question. Talkie tells users their conversations are private. But Together AI, which sells businesses access to a MiniMax text-to-speech model, claimed until last week that it was trained on “Talkie conversation data”.
When we asked Together AI about this, it told us: “MiniMax let us know today that the description of the training data on our webpage was incorrect, and we’ve updated it accordingly.” Neither company has explained what training data was used.
MiniMax has separately described using data collected from “interactions with [its] other services or products” to improve one of its AI models. Talkie’s privacy policy, meanwhile, says conversations can be used to improve the service itself, but will not be used for marketing or advertising.
A MiniMax patent describes turning conversations into training material by judging whether users were satisfied, asking questions with the chatbot like: “Did my answer just now offend you?” Another filing describes extracting dating and medical histories from conversations to personalise replies. Neither patent establishes whether these methods are used in Talkie.
Talkie’s privacy policy also allows text and voice conversations to be shared with affiliated companies. And under Chinese law, companies can be required to assist intelligence agencies and hand data over for national security investigations. articles.title_orig: Denny’s celebrates Jensen Huang return to Nvidia: ‘Your booth is waiting’
articles.title_zh: Denny’s celebrates Jensen Huang return to Nvidia: ‘Your booth is waiting’
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia — and Denny's has a booth waiting for him.
The American diner chain welcomed the billionaire's return as Nvidia CEO by revealing that it had reinstated a commemorative plaque marking the birthplace of the artificial intelligence chip giant after learning of its removal on Nov. 13.
"Some things you just don't take off the menu. Jensen Huang is one of them," Denny's said in a post on X .
The plaque marks the booth at a Denny's restaurant in Silicon Valley, California, where Huang and his co-founders discussed the idea for Nvidia, which was founded in 1993.
The restaurant chain said it learned on Nov. 13, a day after Huang's resignation , that the plaque had been removed.
"We put the plaque right back up where it belongs," Denny's said, without specifying who had removed it or why.
Huang's ties to the diner chain, however, stretch back well before Nvidia's founding. He worked at Denny's as a teenager, washing dishes and serving customers before going on to build one of the world's most valuable companies.
The restaurant chain also disclosed that it had contacted Nvidia's communications team on Nov. 10 to express its pride in their shared history.
Huang's return came less than two weeks after his sudden resignation rattled investors and raised questions about corporate governance and succession planning at the chipmaker.
While his return has put those issues in the spotlight, Denny's offered a simpler message to its former employee.
"Jensen, your booth is waiting and the coffee's on. We're always open, 24/7," the restaurant chain said.

articles.title_orig: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights as it faces potential collapse
articles.title_zh: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights as it faces potential collapse
articles.content_orig:
Some holiday travelers woke up this morning to the worst news alert possible — that their flights had been canceled .
Budget airline Norse Atlantic , popular among cost-conscious New Yorkers bound for Europe, ruined Thanksgiving plans for troves of passengers when it suddenly suspended service today — after its stock nearly collapsed amid warnings of financial catastrophe.
“The board of directors continues to consider options to secure short-term financing,” Norse, which closed 85% lower on Wednesday, announced in a statement to CNBC on Thursday. “If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the board’s intention to file for bankruptcy.”
First taking to the skies late in the pandemic era, after it picked up a batch of Boeing 787 Dreamliners that Norwegian Airlines no longer wanted, the cheap carrier blamed surging fuel bills from the Iran war and low supply.
Blaming the Iran war and other reasons for increased costs , Norse was reportedly already operating at reduced capacity and securing less fuel than normal.
As the bad news broke, budget travelers were freaking out.
“Had my Orlando to London flight canceled with less than a day’s notice and of course no effort made on Norse’s behalf to re-route me,” one user recounted on Reddit.
Another flyer on Reddit gearing up for their yearly vacation is likely out of luck.
“I was supposed to travel to Bangkok in two days on my yearly vacation, and return on Dec. 25. That won’t happen now,” the sad flyer wrote in a post .
“Doubtful we’ll ever see transatlantic flights so cheap again,” another traveler added.
The airline was widely celebrated for its low-cost offerings between the United States and Europe.
“Blew my mind how cheap it was,” one person said.
Another wrote, “Sad news for anyone who loves affordable long-haul travel.”
As recently as 2024, the airline was offering $500 business-class-style fares between JFK and London — an unheard-of bargain.
“When I need comfort on a budget and I need it now, it’s great to know there’s an airline that can do that — and apparently still make a dollar or two,” a Post reviewer said at the time .
The shock drop from the schedule isn’t the first hit to traveler wallets this year — in May, Spirit Airlines permanently shut down.
Also known for cheap flights — and zero frills — the company announced it was shutting operations “effective immediately” after failing to secure a $500 million bailout from the federal government.
After Spirit’s trip up to the spirit in the sky, rival Frontier quickly was able to jack prices — reporting an astonishing 71% jump in airfare collected per passenger in the months following.

articles.title_orig: Motorola Signature 27 Shipping Slips to December Amid High Demand
articles.title_zh: Motorola Signature 27 Shipping Slips to December Amid High Demand
articles.content_orig:
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
Since its unveiling on Nov. 5, the Motorola Signature 27 flagship has generated strong demand in the US smartphone market. It’s rare for a phone outside of Apple, Samsung, or Google to create such a buzz, but Motorola has now been forced to delay shipments for some early orders.
Preorders for the Signature 27 began on Nov. 19, with general availability expected Nov. 26. As reported by 9to5Google , the preorder window is still open on Motorola and Best Buy, but the shipment dates there have slipped to Dec. 8 and Dec. 11, respectively.
“We’re excited by the strong consumer response of the new Motorola Signature 27, with demand exceeding our initial expectations. As a result, some orders may experience updated shipping timelines,” Motorola tells 9to5Google. “Our teams are working to meet demand and get devices to customers as quickly as possible.”
The phone became available in Europe on Nov. 16, and the delay in the US market won’t affect all preorders. Some of the buyers will still receive their units on launch date as promised, Android Authority reports .
The demand for Signature 27 is primarily driven by its mind-boggling spec sheet. The $1,600 Motorola flagship runs on the latest 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip and comes in two variants: 12GB RAM/256GB storage or 16GB RAM/512GB storage. Its 6.8-inch display offers a 120Hz adaptive refresh rate and reaches a record-breaking 12,000-nit peak brightness.
The 7,000 mAh battery, meanwhile, promises up to 47 hours of video playback and supports reverse charging. The front camera is 50MP, and the rear setup includes a 50MP main shooter, a 200MP periscope telephoto lens with 100x Super Zoom, and a 50MP ultrawide camera. To top things off, the phone ships with Android 17 out of the box and is slated to receive 7 years of OS and security updates.
Specs aside, users are excited about the phone’s support for GrapheneOS , a privacy-focused Android alternative previously limited to Pixel phones. Some of them are also excited about the phone’s potential to increase competition in the US market.
Jibin is a tech news writer based out of Ahmedabad, India. Previously, he served as the editor of iGeeksBlog and is a self-proclaimed tech enthusiast who loves breaking down complex information for a broader audience.

articles.title_orig: Introducing: Anoma A2, Twisting Cases To Turn Heads
articles.title_zh: Introducing: Anoma A2, Twisting Cases To Turn Heads
articles.content_orig:
Just Because A Ferdinand Berthoud Pièce Unique Eight Years In The Making
The Business of Watches Podcast Fondation Haute Horlogerie Vice-President Pascal Ravessoud
Introducing The Porsche Design Chronograph 1 Utility – Limited Edition for Hodinkee
The second distinct design from Anoma rounds out the brand's offerings. Literally.
In two short years, Anoma has grown into a favorite design-focused microbrand built around its inaugural A1 model . The unusual, triangular design was well-timed for a period of interest in shaped watches and smaller designs, and has served as a strong platform for a range of dials and case treatments. Today, Anoma is growing the product line with the A2, an oval baignoire-style release inspired by a Möbius strip.
The design speaks for itself, with a twisted case that creates an asymmetrical dial opening, machined from a single block of metal using a 5-axis CNC machine. The crystal adds impact, 4mm thick and twisting in the opposite direction for effect. The hands are inspired by Constantin Brancusi’s 1923 "sculpture Bird in Space" and, when set to 10:10, create what Anoma sees as an abstract bird. The stainless case measures 41.5mm x 35.7mm (which the brand says wears like a 38mm round watch) and 9.8mm thick, with a 50m water resistance.
The dial is vertically brushed, and the Anoma nameplate is very reserved. Inside the case is the manually wound La Joux-Perret D100 movement, and while the power reserve wasn't shared, that movement typically offers around 50 hours of power reserve. The crown is hidden around 1:30 on the back of the case (or 10:30 if you're viewing it from the back), keeping the clean, lugless, crownless look intact.
The Anoma A2 is a new part of the brand's core collection, but is available in batches, this time from November 26 to December 3, 2026 on Anoma's website, with deliveries scheduled for April 2027. The retail price is £2,400 or around $3,150.
Anoma's releases have always had a very straightforward but solid impact. As a design-first product, it feels like a part of a tradition going back to Cartier and beyond, that briefly touched all brands (Rolex, Patek—with Gilbert Albert especially—AP, and plenty of others) in the 1940s-1970s. These were never core products for brands, except for Cartier, but they proved that design matters and has a place in watches.
At times, it feels like we're living through a revival that includes brands like Toledano & Chan and Furlan Marri's Disco Volante. You're not buying watches like these for the horological bonafides. You're buying them because they satisfy an urge the market isn't filling. The Anoma A2 slots alongside the Cartier Baignoire in some ways, but it's more sculptural and cheaper. It might be slightly less surprising than the A1, but it also will probably be far more wearable for a lot of people.

articles.title_orig: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
articles.title_zh: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
articles.content_orig:
Relatives and healthcare workers prepare to bury a victim of Ebola, in Beni, North Kivu province, Congo, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP hide caption
BUNIA, Congo — The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Thursday, as fighting between rebels and the army disrupts efforts to contain the spread of the disease.
It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and nearly half the 12,021 people confirmed to have the virus have died, according to data from Congo's Ministry of Health. It is also the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.
The outbreak declared in May is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus , for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Response teams are battling armed conflict, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation .
Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of people who are sick or have died from the disease. Containing the disease requires quickly identifying and treating patients in isolation, monitoring people who may have been exposed and safely burying the dead.
Fighting between the army and the Convention pour la révolution populaire rebels resumed Thursday morning in Iga-Barrière, a mining town about 25 kilometers (15 miles) north of Bunia in eastern Congo, sending new waves of displaced people toward the city. Bunia is the capital of northeastern Ituri province and a major hub for the Ebola response.
CRP is one of more than 100 armed groups in eastern Congo, where conflict has created one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises . The group was founded last year by former warlord Thomas Lubanga, who was convicted by the International Criminal Court in 2012 of recruiting children under 15 and using them in fighting.
Fighting between the army and the rebels earlier this week had already prevented teams from reaching some communities, disrupted monitoring of people exposed to the virus and left some treatment centers with fewer staff, Dr. Catherine Smallwood, the World Health Organization's Ebola incident manager, said Wednesday.
Smallwood said that about a dozen people, including two WHO personnel and Congolese health officials, were evacuated to Bunia on Tuesday after three full days trapped in a hospital in Akwe, northeast of the provincial capital, amid intense crossfire.
